title: Green spaces and new buildings
instructionsHu: Nézd meg a két kép leírását. Írd le és hasonlítsd össze a képeket, fejtsd ki a véleményedet a megadott szempontok alapján, majd beszélgess a vizsgáztatóval a települések fejlődéséről és a zöldterületek védelméről.

scenes.description: On the flat roof of a block of flats in a big city, neighbours of all ages are working in a community garden. Tomatoes, herbs and sunflowers are growing in wooden boxes, and a retired man is showing two children how to water the plants. In the background you can see office towers and cranes. People are chatting and sharing a jug of lemonade.

At the edge of a small town, bulldozers are clearing a field to make room for a new shopping centre and car park. A large sign shows a picture of the finished building with the words 'Opening next year'. Next to the fence, a small group of local residents are holding a banner that says 'Save our green fields'. A few trees have already been cut down, and the ground is muddy.

prompts: Compare the attitudes to land and nature shown in the two pictures.
Why is it important for towns and cities to have green spaces?
How can towns balance economic development and the protection of nature?
followUpQuestions: Are there enough parks and green areas where you live?
Would a new shopping centre be good or bad for a small town? Why?
Do protests by local residents ever change decisions? Can you think of an example?
What would an ideal, environmentally friendly town look like?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text:
Both pictures are about how we use land, but they show opposite attitudes to nature. In the first one, neighbours of all ages are working in a community garden on the roof of a block of flats. Tomatoes and sunflowers are growing in wooden boxes, and an old man is showing two children how to water the plants, with office towers and cranes in the background. The second picture shows bulldozers clearing a field at the edge of a small town to make room for a shopping centre. A few trees have already been cut down, and some local residents are protesting with a banner saying 'Save our green fields'.
So in the first picture people are creating green space even in the middle of a city, whereas in the second, nature is being destroyed for profit. In my opinion, green spaces are essential: they reduce the heat in summer, clean the air and give people a place to meet. Of course, towns need development and jobs, too, but they could build on old industrial sites instead of green fields.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Are there enough parks and green areas where you live?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Not really. Our town has one big park, but the new housing estates have hardly any trees, so in July the concrete gets unbearably hot. I'd love to see more trees planted along the main streets.

notes: Összefüggő témakifejtés: a vizsgázó mindkét képet leírja, az összehasonlításnál megnevezi a lényegi ellentétet (zöldterület teremtése kontra a természet feláldozása a profitért), három érvvel indokolja a zöldfelületek fontosságát, és konkrét kompromisszumot javasol a fejlesztés és a természetvédelem között.
Szókincs: a környezet és a városfejlesztés pontos szavai (community garden, bulldozers, local residents, industrial sites, housing estates) és jó kötőszavak (So, whereas, Of course … but).

Nyelvhelyesség: szenvedő szerkezetek (have already been cut down, is being destroyed), 'whereas', 'could build … instead of' és az 'I'd love to see more trees planted' szerkezet – változatos B2-es nyelvhasználat hiba nélkül.
Érdemes megtanulni: „opposite attitudes to nature”, „nature is being destroyed for profit”, „build on old industrial sites”, „unbearably hot”.
